doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Moving to the Village; Juanita, Jimmy Giuffre and Parkinson's
summary: Russell recounts moving to the Village with Jack's money, Juanita's affair with Jimmy Giuffre, and visiting them each Christmas.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Juanita at that time was – okay. When Jack gave me the album, I took that money and moved – we moved – Juanita and I moved out and moved to the place in the Village. This must have – yeah, okay. Juanita had to be there, in the room with Bill, the
one-room apartment. She had to be a part of it. But when I moved out, it was with Juanita too, but she didn’t stay long, because she and Jimmy had a thing. We still . . .
She’s a fighter. She really – she’s a marvelous woman.
She’s been taking care of Jimmy all these years.
Taking care of – he’s had – what’s this damn crippling disease that men get?
Parkinson’s or one of those syndromes?
I think that’s what Alice has said. That’s terrible, especially for someone who used his hands.
He can’t make any kind of sense. We go up there every – Alice and I go up every Christmas, at least.
They’re good friends, Alice and Juanita. Juanita’s in the family. She’s just great. So this is – as time goes on, eventually Bill had a terrible life.
